notes: This contract pins the bounded embedded federation-save control plane to the exact IEEE 1516.1-2025 C++ RTIambassador and FederateAmbassador declarations exported by the Requirements Lab. It covers initiation, per-federate save acknowledgements, completion/failure, abort, and status response only. The Request Federation Save report lane additionally pins both official C++ overload declarations and their accepted Table 5 argument forms, without expanding its save-admission claim. The new three-member temporal case is limited to an untimed request and stable ordinary time-advance boundaries: each constrained recipient receives Initiate Federate Save directly before its Time Advance Grant, while the non-time-constrained recipient is queued only after all constrained recipients reach that boundary. The paired timed-save contract separately proves the analogous bounded TAR/TARA/NMR/NMRA and strict-actual-FQR behavior. Paired restore-control regressions save a single-federate Non-Regulated-Grant TAR and a pending FQR under HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE, and a six-scenario single-federate matrix saves TARA/NMR/NMRA under both callback models; each restore returns the saved Time Advancing state as a fresh callback-gated grant after Federation Restored. It does not establish untimed Flush Queue Request admission, multi-member advance or FQR restoration, queued/in-transit TSO, role/membership churn, durable snapshots, or complete save/restore semantics. The paired restore-control tests also save a live TSO retraction record, a terminal tombstone, a logical-time/actual-lookahead window, and one deferred lookahead-decrease target, but do not turn this control-plane contract into a complete save/restore claim. Durable snapshot serialization, complete restore semantics, save interlocks across every service, protected review, package support, and conformance remain open.
